title: Chat-CC payload sequencer + idempotency bridge for OpenAI-compatible requests
creator: Aisha Chen
description:
Summary:
Implement a lightweight compatibility layer that converts Redwood's native streaming/tool-calling structured output model into an OpenAI Chat Completions (Chat-CC) request/response shape, while preserving: streaming token deltas, tool/function call semantics, structured outputs, and strong idempotency guarantees across retries. This feature ("payload sequencer + idempotency bridge") is intended for customers who need a drop-in OpenAI Chat Completions web-compatible endpoint backed by Redwood's runtime without losing advanced runtime behaviors (continuous batching, prefix/KV caching, and partial streaming of tool calls).

Goals:
- Correctly map Redwood chat messages and tool call events to the OpenAI Chat Completions streaming SSE/chunked response model so existing OpenAI clients can consume with minimal changes.
- Maintain deterministic idempotency and deduplication across request retries and reconnects (important for function/tool invocations).
- Support structured output formats (JSON schema/response shape) and expose structured-output signals in the Chat-CC "delta" streaming events.
- Introduce minimal latency overhead (target <= 6% p50 token latency increase) and robust telemetry to measure regressions.

Design decisions & trade-offs (summary):
- We will perform mapping at the HTTP gateway layer (stateless translator) rather than modifying the runtime, to simplify rollbacks and make feature-flagging per-customer easier. Trade-off: additional hop but simpler isolation and faster rollout.
- For streaming we will emit OpenAI-style events in the exact sequence our runtime produces tokens/events, but we will batch small contiguous deltas at 50ms windows to avoid tiny-chunk amplification that breaks some clients. Trade-off: small added micro-batching latency vs client compatibility.
- Tool calls will be signaled via Chat-CC's function call object in the finalization event and via interim delta messages that include a partial "tool_call" marker. We avoid inventing new OpenAI protocol fields; instead we encode a compact standardized marker in the delta when an external tool call starts/ends.
- Idempotency: requests may arrive with the OpenAI-style "idempotency_key" header; if absent we generate a canonical request fingerprint. The bridge maintains a short-lived persistent idempotency index (Redis TTL 10m) keyed by fingerprint to guarantee at-most-once delivery to downstream tool hooks. This is necessary to prevent duplicate effects when a client reconnects mid-tool-call.

Acceptance criteria:
- Native Redwood chat requests can be proxied through the compatibility gateway and consumed by an unmodified OpenAI chat client (including stream-mode via chunked responses or event-stream) for at least 5 representative clients (curl, node-openai, python-openai, postman, chrome devtools).
- Tool invocation ordering preserved and no duplicate tool-call webhook invocations observed in automated replay tests (10k synthetic replays with simulated retries).
- Structured JSON outputs validated against provided schemas are delivered in the expected Chat-CC "content" shapes and present as finalization delta with schema metadata headers.
- Latency regression benchmark: p50 token latency increase <= 6% and p95 <= 12% on standard suite (text-gen-small workload).
- End-to-end telemetry surfaced in Console: per-request mapping time, idempotency index hit/miss, tool-call duplication count, and streaming chunk size distribution.

Implementation plan (high-level):
1) Gateway translator service (stateless) that sits in front of runtime route and implements request shaping and response marshalling.
2) Streaming emitter that converts internal token/event stream -> OpenAI SSE/chunk format. Support both chunked-transfer-encoding and text/event-stream.
3) Lightweight idempotency store (Redis) and pluggable fingerprint generator.
4) Tool-call coordinator that intercepts runtime tool events, locks idempotency key, and tracks webhook call state to prevent duplicates.
5) Test harness and compatibility test suite (clients + replay).
6) Incremental rollout via feature flag per-customer with Canary mode (10% traffic), then 50%, then 100%.

Edge cases and notes:
- Large tool outputs: for long tool responses we stream them as multiple Chat-CC deltas with a suffix marker "__tool_chunk_cont" until finalization. Client libraries that expect single function_call->arguments string may need guidance; include migration note.
- Structured output regression: when structured-output checks fail at runtime we will emit a special finalization delta with error_reason and backoff headers. This is to avoid silent payload corruption.
- Backpressure & disconnects: if a client disconnects mid-stream and then reconnects with same idempotency_key, we will replay the last N events from the idempotency store if still available (configurable TTL). This ensures clients can resume deterministic streams for N seconds.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for translator mapping with dozens of message permutations (system/user/assistant + tool call interleaving).
- Integration tests with local runtime using synthetic KV/prefix cache state and an instrumented webhook endpoint to assert at-most-once semantics.
- Fuzzing for malformed OpenAI-shaped requests to ensure translator rejects unsupported fields and returns compatible error codes.
- Load tests to measure latency and chunking behavior at 10k concurrent streaming clients.

Telemetry & observability:
- New Console dashboard panels: "compat-gateway latency", "stream-chunk size histogram", "idempotency hits", "tool-call duplication rate".
- Log formats will include mapping_trace_id and canonical_fingerprint for offline debugging.

Rollout plan:
- Feature flag off by default. Early adopters opt-in via account setting; internal smoke customers enabled for canary.
- Canary: 10% of traffic for 48h; monitor p50/p95 token latency, error rate, duplication_count.
- If no regression, ramp to 50% for 24h, then 100%.

Migration notes for customers:
- Existing OpenAI clients should be able to call the new endpoint without code changes. For clients that rely on function_call.arguments being a single monolithic string, recommend enabling "compat-tool-argument-concat" feature in Console (temporary).
- Document sample request/response mapping in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/COMPAT/OpenAI-CC-Bridge.

Artifacts & links:
- Design doc: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/cc-idempotency-bridge-design
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/8172
- Test harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/compat-tests/tree/cc-sequencer

Open questions to resolve (action items):
- TTL for idempotency store: 10m is provisional. Ops input required about memory impact at scale (action: @Priya to coordinate with infra).
- Exact token micro-batching window (50ms provisional). Request perf team to run sensitivity tests (action: @Liam).
- Security review for storing canonical fingerprints (PII risk) - we will hash+salt fingerprints and store only salted SHA256 (action: security review).
